title: Aircraft Net Force and Acceleration in 1D
learningObjectives: Describe level cruise as weight balanced by lift and drag balanced by thrust.
Compute 1D acceleration from net force and mass using F = m * a.
Predict rise, fall, acceleration, or slowing from lift-minus-weight or thrust-minus-drag.

sources.title: Simplified Aircraft Motion — NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics

evidence.quote: By simplified motion we mean that some of the four forces acting on the aircraft are balanced by other forces

explanations.text: Simplified motion treats one force and one direction at a time while other opposing forces are taken as balanced.

evidence.quote: the weight would be balanced by the lift and the drag would be balanced by the thrust

explanations.text: In steady level cruise, weight is balanced by lift and drag is balanced by thrust, so velocity stays constant.

evidence.quote: Where a is the acceleration, m is the mass of the aircraft, and F is the net force acting on the aircraft.
The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.

explanations.text: Unbalanced force causes acceleration by F = m * a, where net force is lift minus weight or thrust minus drag.

evidence.quote: If the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft will move in the direction of the greater force.

explanations.text: If forces become unbalanced the aircraft moves toward the greater force, for example thrust greater than drag accelerates it.

predictions.prompt: A model aircraft of mass 2 kg has net thrust-minus-drag of 10 N. Predict its acceleration.
A model aircraft of mass 5 kg has net thrust-minus-drag of -15 N. Predict its acceleration.
A model aircraft of mass 10 kg has net thrust-minus-drag of 20 N. Predict its acceleration.
